summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, studying under August Conrady. He held Indology professorships at Leipzig (1928, 1938–1958) and joined the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1943–1980).

Friedrich Wilhelm is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Paul Thieme and completed his Promotion at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich (Privatdozent 1963, professor 1969–1998) and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1957–1964).
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf works in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg (~1992–1999) and the University of Munich (~1999–2014).

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, University of Tübingen, and University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845), and headed the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (~1889–1893) and Karl Foy.

Friedrich Zarncke was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Rostock and the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He later served at Leipzig as Rektor (1852) and full professor (1858), and held a post at Rostock.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1787–1790) and later served as honorary professor at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), director at the University of Vienna (1824), and head at Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Spiegel was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Erlangen, Leipzig, Bonn, and Jena under Rückert, Fleischer, Brockhaus, Kinkel, and Lassen. From 1849 to 1891, he was an extraordinary professor at Erlangen.

Frits Staal was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Madras. He held professorships at Amsterdam (1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who completed his studies and Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1934), the University of Munich (1936–1941), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1845–1852). He served as librarian at Versailles and the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, administrator at the Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885), and member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.
Fu Yan was a scholar in philosophy and Sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College (~1877–1879). He later held posts at Fudan University (~1905–1906) and Peking University (~1912).
Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong (~1943–1949). He later held an academic post at Tunghai University (~1955–1969).
Fujio Oda is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kyushu University (~1953–1961). He held academic posts at Fukuoka University (~1972–2004) and Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Nagoya University in 1991 under Musashi Tachikawa, and studied with Yusho Miyasaka, Zuiho Yamaguchi, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Kaiun Shirodate.

Fumihiko Sueki works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his degrees, including a Ph.D., from the University of Tokyo, studying under Hajime Nakamura, Yoshiro Tamura, and Kyosho Hayashima. He later taught at Tokyo (1986, 1995–2009) and Nichibunken (~2009–2015).

Fumimaro Watanabe studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto (Ph.D. 1976), under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Hammalawa Saddhatissa. He taught at Kindai University (1972–1981, professor from 1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (professor 1987).
Fumio Enomoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1984) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1997–2017).

Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1954–1965) and Taisho University (~1966–1975), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).
